messages:
maya: Heads up — eu-west1 GPU canary got paused. Preemptible nodes were reclaimed mid-rollout and a Helm post-delete hook hung on cleanup, ArgoCD now shows a sync error blocking the rest of the cluster upgrade. @liam can you take?
liam: On it. I see multiple nodes in Terminating in kube-ops-prod-gpu-ptp. `kubectl describe node` shows pods stuck during drain, one holding `helm.sh/release` finalizer.
devon: That finalizer is from the legacy metrics-exporter HelmRelease. The post-delete hook job crashed and never completed, so the release never finished deletion and Argo is waiting.
maya: What's the fastest unblock? Can we force-remove the finalizer and continue the rollout?
liam: Trying `kubectl patch` on the resource; initial attempt targeted svc and was forbidden. Switching to the HelmRelease CR in namespace monitoring: `kubectl get helmreleases -n monitoring` then `kubectl patch helmrelease metrics-exporter -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}' --type=merge`.
devon: Also noticed cluster-autoscaler didn't provision replacements. Nodepool uses preemptible (spot) instances and our TF has `max_unavailable = 0` for this group so it didn't spin new on-demand nodes. Cost team set preemptible in eu-west to save $, but it lowers resilience.
sre-oncall: Incident bot: autoscaling suppressed due to taint mismatch: new nodes come up without `dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule` taint by default, so pods won't get scheduled. Short-term: either remove taint from pods or patch provisioning template so new nodes have correct taint/labels.
maya: Proposed short-term plan: 1) remove finalizer from HelmRelease, 2) manually delete stuck terminating pods, 3) scale nodepool +2 on-demand gpus in eu-west temporarily, 4) re-run ArgoCD sync. Approve?
liam: :thumbsup: doing steps 1 and 2 now. Patched HelmRelease, deleted terminating pods (used `kubectl delete pod <pod> --grace-period=0 --force`).
devon: Helm release history still shows `hook failed: post-delete`. I ran `helm uninstall --keep-history metrics-exporter -n monitoring` and cleaned up the job that was stuck in CrashLoopBackOff. That cleared the hook state.
liam: Triggered a terraform apply override to add 2 non-preemptible g4dn nodes: `terraform apply -var 'use_preemptible=false' -var 'extra_gpu_count=2'`. New nodes are booting and kubelets are registering.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Terraform apply finished successfully (83s). Changed nodepool: +2 g4dn (eu-west1).
maya: ArgoCD sync is now passing, canary resumed. Follow-ups: add a GitOps guard to block preemptible-only nodepools during rolling upgrades, and add a Helm hook timeout (10m) to fail fast instead of indefinitely blocking. Also schedule a cost vs SLA review with finance.
devon: Filed INF-492: "Prevent preemptible-only nodepools from blocking Helm rollouts". Proposed fixes: terraform policy check (deny preemptible-only for critical nodepools), ArgoCD health overrides for hooks, helm post-hook timeout, and doc updates for canary runbooks.
sre-oncall: Agreed. Moving this to postmortems channel for blameless write-up. Recommend short-term cost uplift approval for eu-west critical pools.
argo-bot: ArgoCD: sync completed for app cluster-rollout (monitoring) — health OK.
maya: Thanks all, closing the thread. Keep an eye on autoscaler metrics for the next 2 hours and ping if any regressions.
